dataset_info.name: Medical Emergency Forced Tool Calls Dataset
dataset_info.description: Pure JSON responses for forced tool calling scenarios in Citizen2Responder
dataset_info.purpose: Train model to output pure JSON tool responses when triggered by buttons/commands
dataset_info.note: These conversations train the model to respond with tool call JSON only, without explanatory text

scenarios.description: Generate report for cardiac arrest scenario

content.text: Someone collapsed and isn't breathing. They're unconscious.
This sounds like a cardiac arrest emergency. Let me gather some information to help. Are you able to check if they have a pulse? Feel for their wrist or neck.
I can't feel a pulse. What should I do?

This is a cardiac arrest. Start CPR immediately: 1) Place hands on center of chest 2) Push hard and fast at least 2 inches deep 3) 30 compressions then 2 breaths 4) Continue until help arrives. Are you able to start CPR?
I've started CPR. Generate report

scenarios.description: Generate report for car accident with injuries

content.text: There's been a car accident. Two cars involved, I can see people injured.
I'll help you handle this car accident. First, ensure your safety - are you in a safe location away from traffic? Can you tell me how many people appear injured?
I'm safe. I see three people - one person is bleeding from their head, another is holding their arm, and one seems okay but shaken up.

Good that you're safe. For the person with head bleeding - do not move them, apply gentle pressure with clean cloth if possible. For the arm injury, support the arm if they'll let you. Have you called 911 yet?
Yes, 911 is on the way. Generate report
Someone is choking at a restaurant. They can't speak or breathe.

This is a choking emergency. If they can't speak or breathe, perform the Heimlich maneuver immediately: 1) Stand behind them 2) Arms around waist 3) Make fist above belly button 4) Quick upward thrusts. Are you able to do this?
I did the Heimlich and the object came out. They're breathing now but coughing. Generate report

scenarios.description: Show care instructions for severe bleeding

content.text: Someone cut themselves badly with a kitchen knife. There's a lot of blood.
This is a serious bleeding emergency. Is the person conscious and alert? Can you see how deep the cut is?
They're conscious but the cut is deep on their hand. Blood is flowing steadily.
Apply direct pressure immediately with clean cloth or towel. Elevate the hand above their heart if possible. Do not remove any cloth that becomes soaked - add more on top.
I'm applying pressure. Show care instructions

scenarios.description: Show care instructions for burn injury

content.text: Someone got burned by hot oil while cooking. Their arm is red and blistering.
This sounds like a second-degree burn. How large is the burned area? Is the person in pain?
It's about the size of my palm on their forearm. They're in a lot of pain.
For a palm-sized burn, this needs medical attention. Cool the burn with cool (not ice-cold) running water for 10-20 minutes if possible.
I'm running cool water over it now. Show care instructions

scenarios.description: Show care instructions for allergic reaction

content.text: My friend ate something and now has hives and is having trouble breathing.
This sounds like a severe allergic reaction. Do they have an EpiPen with them? Are they able to speak in full sentences?
They have an EpiPen but haven't used it yet. They can speak but seem short of breath.
Use the EpiPen now - this is anaphylaxis. Remove safety cap, inject into outer thigh, hold for 10 seconds. Call 911 immediately after.
I used the EpiPen and called 911. Show care instructions

scenarios.description: Generate report for fall with head injury

content.text: An elderly person fell down stairs. They hit their head and seem confused.
Head injuries in elderly patients are serious. Are they conscious and responding to you? Can you see any bleeding or obvious injury?
They're awake but keep asking the same questions. I see a small cut on their forehead but not much bleeding.
The confusion and repeated questions suggest possible concussion. Do not move them. Keep them still and awake. Have you called for medical help?
Yes, ambulance is coming. Generate report

scenarios.description: Show care instructions for spinal injury precautions

content.text: Someone fell from a ladder and is on the ground. They can't feel their legs.
This is a potential spinal injury. Do NOT move them at all. Are they conscious and able to speak to you?
Yes, they're awake and talking but scared. They say they can't move their legs.
Keep them calm and completely still. Support their head if needed but do not move their neck. This requires immediate emergency response.
I'm keeping them still. EMS is on the way. Show care instructions
I found someone unconscious with pill bottles nearby. Their breathing is very slow.
This could be a drug overdose. Are you able to wake them up by shouting or gentle shaking? Can you check their pulse?
They won't wake up even when I shake them. Pulse is there but very slow. I called 911.
Good that you called 911. If you suspect opioid overdose, do you have Narcan/naloxone available? Keep monitoring their breathing - be ready to do rescue breathing if it stops.
I don't have Narcan. Their breathing is still slow but steady. Generate report

scenarios.description: Show care instructions for seizure patient

content.text: Someone just had a seizure and is now lying on the ground confused.
Is the seizure still happening or have they stopped convulsing? Are they breathing normally now?
The seizure stopped about a minute ago. They're breathing but seem very confused and sleepy.
This is normal after a seizure - it's called the postictal period. Keep them safe and comfortable while they recover. Do not restrain them or put anything in their mouth.
They're starting to become more aware. Show care instructions
